Package Tour and Data-Shape Conventions

Dereck Mezquita

Source: vignettes/data-shapes.Rmd
data-shapes.Rmd

This vignette is the one-stop tour of the binance package. It catalogues every public method by topic, explains the shape of what each one returns, and then documents the underlying data-shape policy in detail.

If you’ve never used the package, read top to bottom. If you’ve used it and just want to know how a specific endpoint comes back, jump to the catalogue table for its class and then to the relevant treatment section.

The same conventions are shared with the sister alpaca and (in-progress) kucoin packages, so that switching between exchanges does not mean switching mental models of how the data looks.

What’s in the package

Thirteen R6 classes cover the spot, futures, margin, Earn, sub-account, and funding surfaces of the Binance REST API. Every class supports both synchronous and asynchronous (promise-based) operation via httr2.

Class What it covers
BinanceMarketData Spot public market data — server time, exchange info, tickers, 24hr stats, average price, orderbook depth, recent trades, klines
BinanceFuturesData USDⓈ-M futures public market data — exchange info, klines, mark price, funding rate, open interest, tickers, orderbook, trades, index/mark-price klines
BinanceMarginData Cross- and isolated-margin pair info, price index, interest-rate history, cross/isolated margin data
BinanceTrading Spot order management — place, cancel, query (test endpoint included)
BinanceOcoOrders Spot OCO (one-cancels-the-other) order placement, cancellation, queries
BinanceFutures USDⓈ-M futures trading — orders, account, balances, positions, leverage, margin type / margin movement, income history, position mode
BinanceMargin Cross- and isolated-margin trading — borrow / repay, margin orders, account, max borrowable / transferable, interest history, force liquidations, isolated transfers
BinanceAccount Spot account info, balances, user trades
BinanceDeposit Deposit address and deposit history
BinanceWithdrawal Withdrawal submission and withdrawal history
BinanceTransfer Universal asset transfers between wallets (spot, margin, futures, funding) and history
BinanceEarn Simple Earn — flexible and locked products, subscriptions, redemptions, positions, history
BinanceSubAccount Sub-account list, balances, spot summary, universal transfers, futures / margin account summaries, status

Standalone (not on a class):

Helper What it does
get_api_keys(), get_base_url(), get_futures_base_url() Read API credentials and base URLs from environment variables
binance_build_request() Low-level HTTP / signing primitive — every method goes through this
binance_backfill_klines() Bulk historical klines download for many symbols × intervals with CSV resume
verify_symbol() Sanity-check a symbol against exchangeInfo before placing an order
time_convert_to_binance(), time_convert_from_binance() Millisecond timestamps ↔︎ POSIXct

Setup

Set credentials in .Renviron:

BINANCE_API_KEY=your-api-key
BINANCE_API_SECRET=your-api-secret
BINANCE_API_ENDPOINT=https://api.binance.com           # spot / margin / Earn / sub-account
BINANCE_FUTURES_API_ENDPOINT=https://fapi.binance.com  # USDⓈ-M futures

Then in R:

library(binance)
keys     <- get_api_keys()
market   <- BinanceMarketData$new()                 # public, no keys needed
acct     <- BinanceAccount$new(keys = keys)
trading  <- BinanceTrading$new(keys = keys)
futures  <- BinanceFutures$new(keys = keys)
margin   <- BinanceMargin$new(keys = keys)
earn     <- BinanceEarn$new(keys = keys)

BinanceMarketData — spot public market data

Reference data and clock

Method Endpoint Shape
get_server_time() /api/v3/time single row
get_exchange_info(symbol) /api/v3/exchangeInfo one row per symbol, ;-collapsed string arrays (order_types, permissions, allowed_self_trade_prevention_modes, …); flattened numeric filters (lot_min_qty, lot_max_qty, lot_step_size, price_min, price_max, price_tick_size, min_notional); full filters array preserved as JSON in filters_raw; permission_sets JSON-encoded
get_rate_limits() /api/v3/exchangeInfo (rateLimits slice) one row per rate-limit rule
get_exchange_filters() /api/v3/exchangeInfo (exchangeFilters slice) one row per exchange-wide filter (usually empty)

Tickers and 24hr stats

Method Endpoint Shape
get_ticker(symbol) /api/v3/ticker/price single row
get_all_tickers() /api/v3/ticker/price one row per symbol
get_book_ticker(symbol) /api/v3/ticker/bookTicker single row
get_24hr_stats(symbol) /api/v3/ticker/24hr single row
get_all_24hr_stats() /api/v3/ticker/24hr one row per symbol
get_avg_price(symbol) /api/v3/avgPrice single row

Orderbook, recent trades, klines

Method Endpoint Shape
get_depth(symbol, limit) /api/v3/depth one row per (side, price level) — side ∈ {"bid","ask"}, level 1-indexed
get_trades(symbol, limit) /api/v3/trades one row per trade
get_klines(symbol, interval, ...) /api/v3/klines one row per kline 
# Top 5 highest-priced asks
depth <- market$get_depth("BTCUSDT", limit = 5)
depth[side == "ask"][order(-price)][1:5]

BinanceTrading — spot order management

Method Endpoint Shape
add_order(type, symbol, side, ...) POST /api/v3/order one row per fill if new_order_resp_type = "FULL" and the order filled; otherwise a single row with fill_* columns NA (schema-stable)
add_order_test(...) POST /api/v3/order/test single row data.table(validated = TRUE) on success
cancel_order(symbol, ...) DELETE /api/v3/order single row
cancel_all_orders(symbol) DELETE /api/v3/openOrders one row per cancelled order; empty data.table if no open orders
get_order(symbol, ...) GET /api/v3/order single row
get_open_orders(symbol) GET /api/v3/openOrders one row per open order
get_all_orders(symbol, ...) GET /api/v3/allOrders one row per order 
# Long format: one row per fill, parent order fields replicated.
order <- trading$add_order(
  type = "MARKET", symbol = "BTCUSDT", side = "BUY",
  quantity = 0.0001, new_order_resp_type = "FULL"
)
order[, .(order_id, status, fill_index, fill_price, fill_qty)]

BinanceOcoOrders — spot OCO orders

OCO lists are inherently nested (one list contains multiple legs). The package expands the orderReports array to one row per leg with the list-level fields replicated; columns are prefixed order_report_*.

Method Endpoint Shape
add_oco_order(symbol, side, ...) POST /api/v3/order/oco one row per leg (order_report_* columns)
cancel_oco_order(symbol, ...) DELETE /api/v3/orderList one row per cancelled leg (order_report_* columns) — not the cut-down orders array Binance also returns
get_oco_order(...) GET /api/v3/orderList single row (the list itself)
get_open_oco_orders() GET /api/v3/openOrderList one row per open list
get_all_oco_orders(...) GET /api/v3/allOrderList one row per list

Standalone helpers

Credentials and base URLs 

keys     <- get_api_keys()                      # reads .Renviron
spot_url <- get_base_url()                      # api.binance.com
fut_url  <- get_futures_base_url()              # fapi.binance.com

Low-level HTTP

binance_build_request() constructs and signs every request. You should rarely call it directly — every method goes through it — but it’s exported so you can wrap any not-yet-bound endpoint without re-implementing HMAC-SHA256 signing.

Bulk klines download 

# Backfill 5m bars for many symbols, with CSV resume so an aborted run
# doesn't restart from scratch.
binance_backfill_klines(
  symbols  = c("BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT"),
  interval = "5m",
  start    = "2024-01-01",
  end      = "2024-02-01",
  output_dir = "data/klines"
)

Time conversions 

time_convert_to_binance(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC"))
#> [1] 1704067200000
time_convert_from_binance(1704067200000)
#> [1] "2024-01-01 UTC"

Symbol verification 

verify_symbol("BTCUSDT")   # TRUE
verify_symbol("BTCUSDC")   # TRUE
verify_symbol("FOOBAR")    # FALSE, with informative message

Data-shape conventions

The shape policy below is shared with alpaca and kucoin. The guiding rule is:

Identify the entity for the endpoint, and return one row per entity.

A trade gets a row. An order gets a row. An asset balance gets a row. A funding-rate snapshot gets a row. Anything nested under the entity becomes a flat column on the same row or an additional row on a different axis — never a list column — and no data is dropped; fields that don’t fit a per-entity row are surfaced via a sibling method or as an attribute on the returned data.table.

There are five shape treatments. A handful of endpoints use two treatments together when their nesting has two layers.

Treatment A — ; collapse for arrays of plain strings

When a field is an array of short, plain string values (codes, permissions, order types) and the user mostly filters by them or displays the whole list, collapse with ; into a single character column. Filter with grepl, recover the original vector with strsplit(x, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]].

info <- market$get_exchange_info("BTCUSDT")

# An array of plain strings, collapsed into one `;`-separated column:
info$order_types
#> [1] "LIMIT;LIMIT_MAKER;MARKET;STOP_LOSS_LIMIT;TAKE_PROFIT_LIMIT"
#> [2] "LIMIT;MARKET"

# Filter with grepl()
info[grepl("MARKET", order_types)]
#>     symbol  status base_asset base_asset_precision quote_asset
#>     <char>  <char>     <char>                <int>      <char>
#> 1: BTCUSDT TRADING        BTC                    8        USDT
#> 2: ETHUSDT TRADING        ETH                    8        USDT
#>    quote_asset_precision quote_precision base_commission_precision
#>                    <int>           <int>                     <int>
#> 1:                     8               8                         8
#> 2:                     8               8                         8
#>    quote_commission_precision
#>                         <int>
#> 1:                          8
#> 2:                          8
#>                                                   order_types iceberg_allowed
#>                                                        <char>          <lgcl>
#> 1: LIMIT;LIMIT_MAKER;MARKET;STOP_LOSS_LIMIT;TAKE_PROFIT_LIMIT            TRUE
#> 2:                                               LIMIT;MARKET           FALSE
#>    oco_allowed oto_allowed opo_allowed quote_order_qty_market_allowed
#>         <lgcl>      <lgcl>      <lgcl>                         <lgcl>
#> 1:        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE                           TRUE
#> 2:       FALSE       FALSE       FALSE                           TRUE
#>    allow_trailing_stop cancel_replace_allowed amend_allowed
#>                 <lgcl>                 <lgcl>        <lgcl>
#> 1:                TRUE                   TRUE          TRUE
#> 2:               FALSE                  FALSE         FALSE
#>    peg_instructions_allowed is_spot_trading_allowed is_margin_trading_allowed
#>                      <lgcl>                  <lgcl>                    <lgcl>
#> 1:                     TRUE                    TRUE                      TRUE
#> 2:                    FALSE                    TRUE                     FALSE
#>    permissions                   permission_sets
#>         <char>                            <char>
#> 1: SPOT;MARGIN [["SPOT","MARGIN","TRD_GRP_004"]]
#> 2:        SPOT                              <NA>
#>    default_self_trade_prevention_mode   allowed_self_trade_prevention_modes
#>                                <char>                                <char>
#> 1:                       EXPIRE_MAKER EXPIRE_TAKER;EXPIRE_MAKER;EXPIRE_BOTH
#> 2:                               NONE                                  NONE
#>    lot_min_qty lot_max_qty lot_step_size price_min price_max price_tick_size
#>          <num>       <num>         <num>     <num>     <num>           <num>
#> 1:       1e-05        9000         1e-05      0.01     1e+06            0.01
#> 2:          NA          NA            NA      0.01     1e+05            0.01
#>    min_notional
#>           <num>
#> 1:           NA
#> 2:           NA
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                 filters_raw
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                      <char>
#> 1: [{"filterType":"PRICE_FILTER","minPrice":"0.01000000","maxPrice":"1000000.00","tickSize":"0.01000000"},{"filterType":"LOT_SIZE","minQty":"0.00001000","maxQty":"9000.00000000","stepSize":"0.00001000"}]
#> 2:                                                                                                   [{"filterType":"PRICE_FILTER","minPrice":"0.01000000","maxPrice":"100000.00","tickSize":"0.01000000"}]

# Recover the original vector
strsplit(info$order_types[1], ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
#> [1] "LIMIT"             "LIMIT_MAKER"       "MARKET"           
#> [4] "STOP_LOSS_LIMIT"   "TAKE_PROFIT_LIMIT"

Where this is used: exchange_info (spot + futures) for order_types, permissions, allowed_self_trade_prevention_modes, time_in_force, underlying_sub_type. get_account_info for permissions.

The separator is ; rather than , because semicolons are far less likely to appear inside any of the joined values themselves. If Binance ever ships a value that contains ;, the parser emits a once-per-session warning so we catch it immediately rather than silently corrupting data.

Treatment B — Long format for arrays of objects

When the array elements are themselves records (each has multiple fields), explode to one row per element with parent fields replicated. A 1-indexed position column is added where order matters.

# `add_order` returns one row per fill, with the order-level fields
# replicated. `fill_index` runs 1..N.
order <- trading$add_order(
  type = "MARKET", symbol = "BTCUSDT", side = "BUY",
  quantity = 0.0001, new_order_resp_type = "FULL"
)
order[, .(order_id, status, fill_index, fill_price, fill_qty)]
#>    order_id status fill_index     fill_price   fill_qty
#>       <num> <char>      <int>         <char>     <char>
#> 1:       28 FILLED          1 50000.00000000 0.00005000
#> 2:       28 FILLED          2 50001.00000000 0.00005000

# `get_depth` returns one row per (side, price level).
depth <- market$get_depth("BTCUSDT", limit = 5)
depth[, .(side, price, size)]
#>      side   price      size
#>    <char>   <num>     <num>
#> 1:    bid 67232.8 0.4186184
#> 2:    bid 67232.5 1.5000000
#> 3:    bid 67230.0 0.8000000
#> 4:    ask 67232.9 1.2480899
#> 5:    ask 67233.5 0.5000000
#> 6:    ask 67235.0 2.1000000

Where this is used: order fills, OCO orderReports, futures account assets, margin account userAssets, sub-account spotSubUserAssetBtcVoList, orderbook bids / asks, margin marginablePairs.

Schema stability: when the array is empty, the <child>_ columns are still present on the row, filled with NA. So if (any(dt$fill_index == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)) { ... } works whether the order had fills or not.

Treatment C — Wide prefix for fixed-schema nested objects

When the field is a single nested object with a known fixed key set, flatten it to parent_child columns.

info <- acct$get_account_info()

# `commissionRates` was a nested object — now wide-prefixed.
info[, .(commission_rates_maker, commission_rates_taker,
         commission_rates_buyer, commission_rates_seller)]
#>    commission_rates_maker commission_rates_taker commission_rates_buyer
#>                    <char>                 <char>                 <char>
#> 1:             0.00150000             0.00150000             0.00000000
#>    commission_rates_seller
#>                     <char>
#> 1:              0.00000000

Where this is used: get_account_info‘s commissionRates, Earn get_locked_products’ detail_* / quota_*, the extracted numeric filter columns on exchange_info (lot_min_qty, lot_max_qty, lot_step_size, price_min, price_max, price_tick_size, min_notional), isolated-margin base_asset_* / quote_asset_*.

Treatment D — Re-route to a sibling method

When a response bundles a collection that doesn’t fit the per-entity row of the calling endpoint — typically heterogeneous siblings (e.g. account-level fields and balances, or per-symbol rows and exchange-wide rate-limit rules) — the parser keeps only the rows for the entity the method names, and the rest is exposed via a dedicated sibling method. Every method still returns one data.table; no data is lost.

# `BinanceFutures::get_account` returns one row per asset balance.
# Binance also returns a `positions` array alongside `assets`; rather
# than Cartesian-joining them, `positions` is parsed by the dedicated
# method that hits `/fapi/v2/positionRisk`:
fut_acct  <- futures$get_account()    # one row per asset
positions <- futures$get_positions()  # one row per open position
fut_acct
#>    fee_tier can_trade can_deposit can_withdraw update_time multi_assets_margin
#>       <int>    <lgcl>      <lgcl>       <lgcl>       <int>              <lgcl>
#> 1:        0      TRUE        TRUE         TRUE           0               FALSE
#>    total_initial_margin total_maint_margin total_wallet_balance
#>                  <char>             <char>               <char>
#> 1:           0.00000000         0.00000000        1000.00000000
#>    total_unrealized_profit total_margin_balance total_position_initial_margin
#>                     <char>               <char>                        <char>
#> 1:              0.00000000        1000.00000000                    0.00000000
#>    total_open_order_initial_margin total_cross_wallet_balance
#>                             <char>                     <char>
#> 1:                      0.00000000              1000.00000000
#>    total_cross_un_pnl available_balance max_withdraw_amount asset_asset
#>                <char>            <char>              <char>      <char>

# `/exchangeInfo` bundles per-symbol rows + exchange-wide rate-limit
# rules + exchange-wide filter rules. Per-symbol stays on the main
# method; the rest moves to siblings.
info        <- market$get_exchange_info()       # one row per symbol
rate_limits <- market$get_rate_limits()         # one row per rate-limit rule
ex_filters  <- market$get_exchange_filters()    # one row per exchange-wide filter (usually empty)

The cases:

  • BinanceFutures::get_account() re-routes positions to get_positions().
  • BinanceAccount::get_account_info() re-routes balances to get_balances() (both methods hit /api/v3/account; they just parse different halves of the response).
  • get_exchange_info() (spot + futures) re-routes rateLimits to get_rate_limits(), exchangeFilters to get_exchange_filters(), and (futures only) assets to get_futures_assets(). The constant scalars (timezone = "UTC", futures_type = "U_M") and serverTime (already in get_server_time()) are not re-exposed.

Treatment E — JSON string for dynamic-key or array-of-array objects

When a nested object has dynamic keys (different products have different key sets) or is an array of arrays where the inner grouping carries semantic meaning, neither ;-collapse nor wide-prefix preserves the structure. Serialise the whole field as a JSON string; recover with jsonlite::fromJSON.

# spot exchangeInfo `permissionSets` is an array of arrays — each
# inner array is an alternative permission set the user can satisfy.
# `;`-joining would collapse `[["A","B"]]` and `[["A"],["B"]]` to
# the same `"A;B"`, losing the grouping.
info <- market$get_exchange_info("BTCUSDT")
info$permission_sets
#> [1] "[[\"SPOT\",\"MARGIN\",\"TRD_GRP_004\"]]"
#> [2] NA

# Recover the structure
jsonlite::fromJSON(info$permission_sets[1], simplifyVector = FALSE)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> [1] "SPOT"
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> [1] "MARGIN"
#> 
#> [[1]][[3]]
#> [1] "TRD_GRP_004"
# Earn `tierAnnualPercentageRate` has dynamic keys per product
# (different size tiers).
products <- earn$get_flexible_products(asset = "USDT")
products$tier_annual_percentage_rate
#> [1] "{\"0-5BTC\":0.05,\"5-10BTC\":0.03}"

tiers <- jsonlite::fromJSON(products$tier_annual_percentage_rate[1])
tiers
#> $`0-5BTC`
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $`5-10BTC`
#> [1] 0.03

Where this is used: spot exchangeInfo permission_sets, Earn get_flexible_products / get_flexible_position’s tier_annual_percentage_rate.

Two cross-cutting rules

These apply to every shape treatment:

  1. Empty / null array → NA_character_ (no list cells). An asset with no attributes returns attributes = NA, not attributes = list().
  2. Empty response → empty data.table (no synthetic stub rows). cancel_all_orders() with no open orders returns a zero-row table, not a 1-row (symbol, status = "cancelled") fabrication. The absence of an error is the success signal.

What was not done

A few intentional non-goals, mirroring the alpaca package:

  • No automatic numeric coercion of “string-numeric” fields. Binance returns prices, quantities, and commissions as fixed-precision strings; the package preserves them as character so the user controls precision. Cast with as.numeric() at the point of use.
  • No automatic local-time conversion. Timestamps come back as UTC POSIXct. Convert with format(x, tz = "America/New_York") or similar at display time.
  • No client-side rate-limiting. The package surfaces Binance’s X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT headers in errors but does not back off on its own — that is the caller’s job.
  • No reconnect / retry on transient network errors. The single call is what you asked for; wrap with httr2::req_retry() (passed through binance_build_request()) if you want retries.

Why this matters across exchanges

The alpaca, binance, and (in-progress) kucoin packages all follow the same shape rule. That means once you’ve learned data.table idioms for one of them, the same idioms work on the others — pivot a portfolio’s mark-prices across both exchanges with a straight rbind plus an exchange column, no per-source shape massage.

# Combine spot + futures + margin balances into one ledger
ledger <- rbind(
  acct$get_balances()[,         wallet := "spot"],
  futures$get_balances()[,      wallet := "usdtm"],
  margin$get_account()[,        wallet := "margin"],
  fill = TRUE
)
ledger[as.numeric(free) > 0]
